01.heroSub: Transforming manual matchmaking into a streamlined digital workflow
01.overview: Sababa & All is a matchmaking platform for a community organisation. The team was drowning in spreadsheets, sticky notes and WhatsApp threads — I turned it into a focused digital workflow that the team actually adopted.
01.challenge: The matchmaking coordinators juggled dozens of active connections per week using scattered tools. Information was duplicated, privacy was at risk, and onboarding a new coordinator meant weeks of tribal knowledge transfer.

process.title: Discovery
process.text: Shadowed coordinators for a week. Mapped every touchpoint from first contact to successful match. Identified 11 distinct friction points.

process.title: UX Design
process.text: Designed a privacy-first card system with status pipelines. Ran 3 rounds of low-fi testing with the team before moving to high-fidelity.

process.title: Build & Launch
process.text: Built with Claude Code. Launched in 2 weeks, iterated in 3 sprints based on real coordinator feedback.

01.outcome: The platform replaced every spreadsheet and group chat. All three coordinators use it daily with zero training overhead.

02.heroSub: AI-assisted shift scheduling for therapeutic and residential care teams
02.overview: ShiftWise replaces the weekly spreadsheet ritual for care team managers. It handles availability, swaps, and fairness rules — so managers spend time on care, not logistics.
02.challenge: Scheduling for a therapeutic team is not just about filling slots. It requires balancing clinical qualifications, personal availability, staff wellbeing, and regulatory fairness rules — all at once, every week.

process.title: Research
process.text: Interviewed 8 care team managers across 3 organisations. Found that 4+ hours per week were lost to scheduling alone.

process.title: System Design
process.text: Mapped the fairness rules into an algorithm. Designed constraint-based scheduling with override capability for edge cases.

process.title: Validation
process.text: Piloted with one team for 6 weeks. Iterated on the swap request flow and the manager approval interface.

02.outcome: Scheduling time dropped dramatically. Staff reported higher satisfaction — the system is transparent and fair, which matters as much as the time saved.

03.heroSub: Medication management for a Jerusalem Soteria house — from 5% errors to zero
03.overview: Balance is a medication tracking system designed for a supportive living environment in Jerusalem. The existing process — handwritten logs and verbal handoffs — produced a 5% error rate. The redesign brought it to 0%.
03.challenge: Three distinct user personas (residents, house staff, and a supervising clinician) all interact with the medication process differently. A single interface could not serve all three — the system needed to adapt to each role without adding complexity.

process.title: Persona Mapping
process.text: Ran contextual interviews with all three user types. Built distinct journey maps and identified where errors occurred in the handoff chain.

process.title: Error Analysis
process.text: Categorised the 5% errors: 60% were timing errors, 30% were dosage misreadings, 10% were missed signatures. Designed against each category.

process.title: 3-Screen System
process.text: Built with Base44. Each persona gets a tailored view. Cross-role confirmations create a closed loop that prevents silent errors.

03.outcome: Medication errors dropped from 5% to 0% within the first month. All three user groups report the system feels natural for their role.

04.heroSub: An interactive Bible learning app — study, exploration, and AI-powered conversation
04.overview: BibleConnect was built for the '929' community project, which reads one Bible chapter per day across Israel. The app makes the text personal, searchable, and alive through AI-powered conversation and community commentary.
04.challenge: Ancient text in a modern interface risks two failure modes: making it feel like a museum exhibit, or making it feel shallow. The design challenge was to honour the depth of the source material while making it genuinely accessible to a secular, digital-native audience.

process.title: Content UX
process.text: Mapped how different readers engage with sacred text — linear readers, explorers, and community participants. Designed for all three modes.

process.title: AI Conversation Design
process.text: Crafted the conversational AI persona — knowledgeable but humble, surfacing context without moralising. Iterated on 40+ conversation starters.

process.title: Community Layer
process.text: Designed the commentary system so personal annotations and shared insights coexist without competition. Launched with a seed community of 120 users.

04.outcome: Daily active engagement exceeded projections. Users report spending 2× longer with the text than with the print edition — the AI conversation layer is the most-used feature.
